_note: Steel P4 guidance, extracted from the broker digests 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-06.
WHY THIS FILE DID NOT EXIST UNTIL 2026-08-25, which is the whole answer to
'why is guidance withheld': nothing was wrong and no data was missing. The
steel #tags were added to extract/guidance_candidates.py the same day the
sector was built, and the candidate scan finds 7 / 2 / 3 / 3 commitment
sentences for tata / jsw / jindal / sail. The L1 extraction step was simply
never run, so `guidance` had no steel rows and run_scores correctly wrote
'no open guidance' for all four. A withheld pillar because nobody ran the
loader looks identical, from inside the store, to a withheld pillar because
the source is silent.
ONLY MANAGEMENT COMMITMENTS ARE HERE. load_guidance.py rejects any row whose
source_actor is not 'management', and it is right to: a broker restating a
rating says nothing about whether management hits its numbers. Several
candidate sentences were DROPPED for exactly this reason, and they are the
ones that read most like guidance:
'FY27-29 EBITDA +4-13% on better India NSR/coal guidance'  -> Emkay's
ESTIMATE revision, not a company commitment.
'Cautious on FY27 volume guidance execution'               -> Emkay's
opinion ABOUT a guide. Kept as EVIDENCE against SAIL's volume
commitment, which is what it actually is.
'Tata Steel aims to raise value-added ferro alloys share to 70-80%'
-> management, but NO PERIOD and no baseline, so it can never resolve.
A commitment that cannot be graded is not a commitment.
THE JSW ROW IS ALREADY RESOLVED AND IT IS A MISS. Management guided coking
coal cost inflation of $12-15/t and the print came in at +$17/t, which the
digest itself flags as 'above $12-15 guide'. That is the first resolved
commitment in the steel book and the only reason P4 can start accumulating a
track record rather than sitting on the NEUTRAL_PRIOR of 0.5.

TWO QUOTES WERE MIS-ATTRIBUTED IN THE FIRST DRAFT AND A VERIFIER CAUGHT THEM, which is worth recording because neither would have shown up downstream: the schema only enforces that a quote is NON-EMPTY, not that it appears in the source it names (SILENT_BUGS entry 6, the same gap). Jindal's '14% volume CAGR' evidence was dated 30-07 and is in 26-07; SAIL's Tasra evidence said 'Coking coal cost to fall' where the digest says 'costs'. Both now pass a substring check of every quote against the digest it cites. Run that check before loading any hand-built extraction.
